features.headline: USMNT's Balogun does 'Dame Time' celebration after goal vs. Haiti
features.desc: After the star forward found the back of the net against Haiti, he had a specific celebration in mind: Damian Lillard's iconic "Dame Time" motion.
body: It was Dame Time for USMNT striker Folarin Balogun on Saturday.

The U.S. attack rolled against Haiti in the first leg of the two nations' Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie, producing six goals for a 6-0 rout. The last of that scoring barrage came off the foot of Balogun, who entered the game off the bench in the 66th minute before scoring in the 82nd.

And after the star forward found the back of the net, he had a very specific celebration in mind: Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard's iconic "Dame Time" motion. Balogun pointed to his wrist repeatedly as he ran toward a gaggle of USMNT substitutes in celebration.
Following the game, Balogun took to X to further underscore his tribute, posting a clip of the celebration and a photo of Lillard doing the motion.
It wasn't the only time Balogun brought out the celebration on Saturday afternoon — the forward had also done the motion after a 75th-minute goal, but that tally was disallowed after a VAR review.

It's also not the first time Balogun has turned to memorable NBA celebrations for inspiration after scoring. After he opened the scoring for the U.S. against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the World Cup round of 32, Balogun did LeBron James' "silencer"
motion. Coincidentally, that celebration also became official on the second attempt — he had done it on a prior disallowed goal in that game, too.

features.headline: Ranking the top 10 Super Bowl performances by a defender
features.desc: Not all Super Bowl MVPs were quarterbacks or offensive stars. We listed 10 standout individual defensive performances.
body: Super Bowls are mostly remembered for offensive fireworks, miraculous fourth-quarter drives, gravity-defying catches and MVP quarterbacks who hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy in victory.
Yet, as the old adage in football reminds us, offense sells tickets while defense wins championships.

While team defenses such as the 1985 Chicago Bears, 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 2013 Seattle Seahawks dominated as collective units, a select group of defenders delivered singular, dominant, game-altering performances on the NFL's biggest stage.
Here are 10 of the best individual defensive performances in Super Bowl history, including four defenders who earned the game's Most Valuable Player award.
COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February.

We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series, featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027.
Stats: 2.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 pass defended
Miller set the tone with a strip-sack of Cam Newton in the first quarter that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown to give the Broncos a 10-0 lead.

With Denver up 16-10 late in the fourth quarter, Miller once again jarred the ball loose from Newton when he sacked the quarterback deep in Carolina territory to put the Broncos in position to score the game-sealing touchdown four plays later.
Miller's performance was so dominant he earned unanimous Super Bowl MVP honors, becoming the 10th defensive player and fourth linebacker in NFL history to win the award.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason.

The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout — he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season — is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite.
His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate.
Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player).

features.headline: 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!
features.desc: Who is the best soccer player in the world at the November international break? ESPN's latest rankings are here.
body: For as much as I make fun of the Ballon d'Or process and how ridiculous the mushy, vague, contradictory criteria are, I think the voting journalists have probably gotten it right in each of the past three years. At least, they haven't gotten it wrong.

When I wrote up my theoretical ballots in each of the past three years, my three choices were Rodri, Ousmane Dembélé and Harry Kane — the three eventual winners. Once you move beyond the top pick, though, things start to get really weird.
Imagine watching the 2025-26 Premier League season and then finding out that Chelsea's Marc Cucurella got more Ballon d'Or votes than Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhães and William Saliba — combined.
Since the award tends to identify one of the best players on one of the best teams in the world, it does tend to identify a worthy winner. But it rarely identifies any other worthy winners.
Remember when Mohamed Salah led the Premier League in goals and assists two seasons ago for a dominant Liverpool team? He finished fourth, with a vote total closer to 30th than first.
Who, then, is the best player in the world right now? Or rather, who are the best players in the world right now?

In August, we launched the 10 Best List, a recurring look at who I'd estimate to be the — you got it — 10 best soccer players in the world. We're back, post-Harry Kane Ballon d'Or, to update the list.

As a reminder, I'm using this as my guidance: "If you added this player to an average round-of-16 Champions League team, how much more likely would the team be to win the tournament?" And if a player is injured or has been injured recently, I'm dropping him out of the top 10.

features.headline: Who has won the MLB MVP Award? All-time winners list
features.desc: MLB's MVP Award is given to top players in the American League and National League. Take a look at the all-time winners list now.
body: There are two MVPs in Major League Baseball each year — one in the American League and one in the National League. Since 1931, the Baseball Writers' Association of America has voted for the MVPs at the end of the regular season and before the start of the postseason.
The award began in 1911 as the Chalmers Award, honoring the "most important and useful player to the club and to the league." That award was discontinued in 1914.

From 1922 to 1928 in the AL and from 1924 to 1929 in the NL, the League Award was presented to "the baseball player who is of the greatest all-around service to his club." Prior winners were not eligible to win the award again during that time.

In 2026, Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros won MVP for the American League, the 3rd Astros player to win the award after Jose Altuve in 2017 and Jeff Bagwell in 1994. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs won for the National League, the first Cubs player to win it since Kris Bryant in 2016.
Take a look at all-time AL and NL MVP award winners below:
2026: Yordan Alvarez (AL), Pete Crow-Armstrong (NL)
2023: Shohei Ohtani (AL), Ronald Acuna Jr. (NL)
2022: Aaron Judge (AL), Paul Goldschmidt (NL)
2018: Mookie Betts (AL), Christian Yelich (NL)
2017: Jose Altuve (AL), Giancarlo Stanton (NL)
2013: Miguel Cabrera (AL), Andrew McCutchen (NL)
2008: Dustin Pedroia (AL), Albert Pujols (NL)
2007: Alex Rodriguez (AL), Jimmy Rollins (NL)
2005: Alex Rodriguez (AL), Albert Pujols (NL)
2004: Vladimir Guerrero (AL), Barry Bonds (NL)
1999: Iván Rodríguez (AL), Chipper Jones (NL)
